column3: The Trinity UFO Crash Pt 1: Because it was Getting Late
column5: In August 1945, near San Antonio, New Mexico, two boys searching for a lost cow reportedly stumbled on a crashed craft close to the Trinity atomic test site. The case predates Roswell by almost two years and was nearly lost to history until Paola Leopizzi Harris and Jacques Vallée revived it.

column3: What is the Story Behind the Georgia Guidestones
column5: The Georgia Guidestones were a granite monument carved with ten cryptic 'commandments' whose meaning was long guessed at and widely condemned. Their secretive creator, 'R.C. Christian', actually wrote a 100-plus-page book explaining exactly what they meant.

On the night of September 1, 1969, rural Berkshire County in Massachusetts saw upwards of 40 UFO events. People were reportedly abducted in view of witnesses and cars were forced off the road by huge hovering craft.

column3: The Andreasson Affair Pt 1: It's Like A Whirlpool
column5: Betty Andreasson's 1967 abduction from her Massachusetts home is one of the most heavily documented UFO cases on record. It was backed by Dr. J. Allen Hynek and scrutinised almost as intensely as the story itself.

column3: The Pemex UFO Incident: UFOs, Humanoids, Cryptids, Weather Manipulation
column5: On June 1, 1973, Ciudad Pemex in Tabasco, Mexico experienced a UFO flap, close contact, cryptid sightings and a government clean-up crew. Despite the many witnesses, it remains one of the best-kept secrets in UFO history.

In 1803 a strange round vessel carrying a mysterious woman reportedly washed ashore on the coast of Japan. Accounts of the Utsuro-bune leave open whether it was an early close encounter or just a historical oddity.
Asheville, North Carolina has a long list of local ghost stories and haunted buildings. This is a tour of some of the city's best-known hauntings.

column3: The Mojave UFO Incident Pt 1: Guards & Gremlins
column5: On October 21, 1989, a couple driving through an empty stretch of the Mojave Desert had a terrifying encounter with a UFO and strange guards. It is an abduction story that is hard to compare with any other experiencer account.

column3: Coral Castle: One Man Unlocks the Truth Behind the Pyramids
column5: Ed Leedskalnin single-handedly built Coral Castle in Florida from massive coral blocks, working alone and in secret. How he did it is still debated, with theories ranging from earth energies to alien techniques to lost knowledge.

column3: The Trumbull County UFO Chase! Police & Citizen Recordings From That Night!
column5: On December 14, 1994, a massive UFO appeared about 50 feet above a neighbourhood in Trumbull County, Ohio. Calls flooded in from citizens and police across several townships as officers chased it through the night.

column3: The Van Meter Visitor: Old-Timey Mothman Terrorizes an Old-Timey Town
column5: For five days in 1903, the town of Van Meter, Iowa was terrorised by a huge winged creature with a glowing horn. The townsfolk responded by forming an armed mob to ambush the beast.

In November 1989, Linda Cortile said she was floated out of her 12th-floor apartment in lower Manhattan into a hovering UFO. Astonishingly, credible eyewitnesses near the Brooklyn Bridge claimed to have seen it happen.

column3: Smoky Mountain National Park Disappearances and Mysteries
column5: Great Smoky Mountains National Park has a long record of strange disappearances, including children who vanished without a trace. Its mysteries range from the Cherokee legend of Spearfinger to a possible UFO crash.

column3: The Darwin UFO Flap: 15 Years of USOs, UFOs & Orbs
column5: For about 15 years, the skies and waters around Darwin, Australia produced a run of UFO, USO and orb sightings. The records of the flap stayed buried in obscure government files for over a decade.

column3: When UFOs Kill: The Melting Man of Brazil
column5: In 1946, in Araçariguama, Brazil, João Prestes came home after being struck by a mysterious beam of light, and his flesh began to fall away from his bones. Ufologists later uncovered a web of eerie events around the 'Melting Man' death in this hotspot of high strangeness.

column3: The Benders: American Frontier Family Serial Killers
column5: In the early 1870s, the Bender family ran a roadside inn on the southeast Kansas frontier, and four of them were murderers. Travellers who stopped there began disappearing.

column3: Herbert Baumeister: I-70 Strangler and Fox Hollow Farm Murderer
column5: Herbert Baumeister is suspected of being the I-70 Strangler, who left bodies along the interstate. He is linked to the remains of at least eleven men found buried at his Fox Hollow Farm estate in Westfield, Indiana.

column3: The Tilton UFO Incident: Lost Police Recordings of a Close Encounter
column5: In 1974, police officers in Tilton, New Hampshire radioed in a live close encounter with a UFO that seemed to signal back to them. The recording was nearly lost to time before being remastered.

In December 1978, pilots, a TV news crew and military personnel saw and filmed strange lights off the coast of Kaikoura, New Zealand. The sightings drew international attention and claims of a cover-up, and changed the witnesses' lives.

Paul Schäfer, a German preacher tied to William Branham, used his followers' money to found Colonia Dignidad, a secretive cult colony in rural Chile. It began as a youth home and grew into a sealed-off compound.

column3: Sweep Clear 5: The Shelburne Harbor Incident
column5: In 1967, navy divers near Shelburne, Nova Scotia reportedly watched two unknown craft underwater during a secret operation called Sweep Clear 5. The encounter was nearly lost until researcher Chris Styles spent 30 years uncovering it.

column3: The Lumberton Report: The Earliest Modern Mass Sighting of a Triangle UFO
column5: From April 3 to 9, 1975, more than 80 people around Lumberton, North Carolina, over 40 of them police, saw a triangular UFO. There were high-speed chases and close encounters, and investigator Lee Spiegel got multiple close views.

column3: DC Long, Range 19: The DUMB Dump
column5: In 2010, Army Ranger DC Long went with his father, a Defense Department contractor, to a job site near Fort Bragg called 'Range 19'. They were escorted into an underground facility where a giant granite slab hung silently in midair.

column3: Billy 'Baldy' Mitchell and The Feud of Mitchell's Bend
column5: In 1870s Hood County, Texas, a quarrel between the Mitchell and Truitt families at Mitchell's Bend on the Brazos River turned deadly. It escalated into years of hiding and revenge killings, with Billy 'Baldy' Mitchell at the centre.

column3: The Curse of Palmyra Atoll: Prologue to Sea Wind Murders
column5: Palmyra Atoll is a remote Pacific island with a history of shipwrecks, pirate legends such as the treasure ship La Esperanza, and unexplained disappearances. Its dark reputation, the so-called Palmyra Curse, sets the stage for the 1974 Sea Wind murders.

On the evening of September 12, 1952, a bright object streaked across the sky and seemed to land on a hillside on G. Bailey Fisher's farm in Flatwoods, West Virginia. A group of locals who climbed up to look reported a towering, glowing-eyed figure and a choking mist, and the sheriff later found only a lingering smell.

column3: Entities of St. Ignatius Hospital with Tour Guide, Val Gregory
column5: St. Ignatius Hospital in Colfax, Washington, opened in 1893 and served the Palouse for decades before closing for good. Since then, reports of apparitions and voices in its empty halls have made it known as one of the most haunted buildings in the Pacific Northwest.

column3: A Conversation with Bruce Burnett, Creator of the Tombstone Wild West Paracon, Pt I
column5: Tombstone, Arizona, the silver-boom town of the Earp brothers and the O.K. Corral gunfight, is said to be one of the most haunted towns in the Old West. Visitors and residents report encounters such as a woman in white along its historic streets.

column3: A Conversation with Bruce Burnett, Creator of the Tombstone Wild West Paracon, Pt II
column5: The Bird Cage Theatre opened in 1881 as Tombstone's notorious saloon, gambling hall and brothel, and its walls still carry bullet holes from the gunfights inside. It is now regarded as one of Arizona's most haunted buildings, with reports of phantom music, voices and figures.

On August 13, 1956, radar operators at RAF Lakenheath and RAF Bentwaters tracked unexplained targets and strange aerial lights for about six hours, and fighter jets were scrambled to intercept. Investigators including Project Blue Book and the Condon Committee could not explain it, and anomalous propagation and the Perseid meteors have both been ruled out.

column3: Halloween Bonus; A Powerful, Polish Poltergeist with Translator of The Elusive Force, Joel Stern
column5: In spring 1983, poltergeist activity erupted around a girl named Joasia Gajewski at her family's home in Sosnowiec, Poland, with objects moving and flying on their own. Polish scientists studied the phenomena for some 40 months, making it one of the best documented poltergeist cases.

column3: A Conversation with Paranormal Investigator & Owner of the Knight House, Eric Freeman Sims
column5: The Knight House, built around 1815 to 1820, is the oldest home in Hopkinsville and Christian County, Kentucky, and may have served as a Civil War hospital and an Underground Railroad stop. It has secret tunnels and a door said to be meant for the dead, and its owners report ongoing paranormal activity.

column3: A Conversation with Paranormal Investigator & Owner of The Boyd House, Jill Shelley
column5: The Boyd House is an old home in the tiny town of Boyd in southwest Minnesota, now rented out for overnight stays to people drawn by its reputation. Paranormal investigators have reported apparitions and voices there, and it is billed as one of the most haunted homes in Minnesota.

column3: A Conversation with Paranormal Quest Investigator and Haunted Museum Owner, Steve Hummel
column5: Moundsville, West Virginia, is home to the former West Virginia State Penitentiary, a Gothic prison notorious for violence and executions and now a famous ghost-hunting site. Nearby, the Archive of the Afterlife museum displays haunted and occult objects collected by local investigators.

column3: A Conversation with Silverstar Mountain Sasquatch Photographer, Randee Chase
column5: On November 17, 2005, a hiker on a snowy peak of Silver Star Mountain in Washington's Gifford Pinchot National Forest photographed what appears to be a large, dark, two-legged figure. The photos became one of the region's best-known pieces of Bigfoot evidence.

column3: The Ghost We Made (The Philip Experiment and the Power of Belief)
column5: In the early 1970s, members of the Toronto Society for Psychical Research invented a fictional ghost named Philip, complete with a tragic backstory, to test whether belief alone could produce phenomena. Within months their séance table was rapping out answers and moving on its own, raising questions about thought forms and poltergeists.
